findings.rule: Heat treatment field must not be blank when a heat-treatment note is specified on the drawing.
findings.reasoning: The title block heat_treatment field is '---' while note N1 explicitly requires through hardening to 50 HRC, creating a direct contradiction that could cause the part to be manufactured without any heat treatment.
findings.correction: Update the title block heat_treatment field to reference N1 or state 'Through Hardened 50 HRC' so it matches the note.

findings.rule: Material and heat treatment specification must be metallurgically compatible.
findings.reasoning: 20MnCr5 is a low-carbon case-hardening steel (approx. 0.2% C) designed for carburizing; it cannot be 'through hardened' to 50 HRC because its carbon content is too low to achieve that core hardness via quenching alone.
findings.correction: Either change the material to a medium-carbon or alloy steel suitable for through hardening (e.g., 42CrMo4, EN8), or change the heat treatment in N1 to carburize and harden with an appropriate case/core hardness specification.

findings.rule: Functional diameters on a sleeve (OD mounting surface, ID bore) require explicit tolerances or fit classes.
findings.reasoning: The outer diameter ⌀30 (D1, D13) and inner bore ⌀20 (D4, D12) have no tolerances assigned. As functional surfaces of a pin sleeve, relying on the general machining tolerance of ±0.5 mm (for the 6–30 mm range) or ±0.8 mm (for 30–120 mm range) is far too loose for proper assembly and fit.
findings.correction: Add appropriate tolerances or fit classes (e.g., h6/H7) to the functional outer and inner diameters.
